# Connection Requests API

This file defines the API endpoints for managing connection requests within the application. It handles sending new requests, reviewing pending requests, and ensures all operations are authenticated.

## Overview

The `requests.js` file is part of the `routes` directory and exposes endpoints related to user connection requests. It leverages middleware for authentication and interacts with the `ConnectionRequestModel` and `User` models to manage request data and user information. This module is crucial for facilitating user-to-user interactions and relationship building within the platform.

## Sending a Connection Request

This endpoint allows a user to send a connection request to another user with a specified status.

### `POST /request/send/:status/:toUserId`

Initiates a connection request from the authenticated user to another user.

<ParamField name="status" type="string" required>
  The initial status of the connection request. Allowed values are:
  <InlineList type="bullet">
    <li>`ignored`</li>
    <li>`interested`</li>
  </InlineList>
</ParamField>

<ParamField name="toUserId" type="string" required>
  The unique identifier of the user to whom the request is being sent.
</ParamField>

<ParamField name="userAuth" type="middleware">
  This middleware ensures that the request is authenticated and the `req.user` object is available.
</ParamField>

<RequestExample>
```bash cURL
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/request/send/interested/60c72b2f9b1e8a001f8e4c9d \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN"
```
</RequestExample>

<ResponseExample>
```json 200 OK
{
  "message": "John is interested in Jane",
  "data": {
    "_id": "60c72b2f9b1e8a001f8e4c9e",
    "fromUserId": "60c72b2f9b1e8a001f8e4c9c",
    "toUserId": "60c72b2f9b1e8a001f8e4c9d",
    "status": "interested",
    "createdAt": "2023-10-27T10:00:00.000Z",
    "updatedAt": "2023-10-27T10:00:00.000Z"
  }
}
```
```json 400 Bad Request
{
  "message": "Invalid status type: unknown"
}
```
```json 400 Bad Request
{
  "message": "Connection Request Already Exists"
}
```
```json 404 Not Found
{
  "message": "User not found!"
}
```
</ResponseExample>

<Note>
  The `sendEmail` utility is commented out in the source code. If uncommented, it would attempt to send an email notification upon successful request creation.
</Note>

## Reviewing a Connection Request

This endpoint allows a user to review a pending connection request sent to them.

### `POST /request/review/:status/:requestId`

Updates the status of a received connection request.

<ParamField name="status" type="string" required>
  The review status for the connection request. Allowed values are:
  <InlineList type="bullet">
    <li>`accepted`</li>
    <li>`rejected`</li>
  </InlineList>
</ParamField>

<ParamField name="requestId" type="string" required>
  The unique identifier of the connection request to review.
</ParamField>

<ParamField name="userAuth" type="middleware">
  This middleware ensures that the request is authenticated and the `req.user` object is available. The authenticated user must be the `toUserId` of the request.
</ParamField>

<RequestExample>
```bash cURL
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/request/review/accepted/60c72b2f9b1e8a001f8e4c9e \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN"
```
</RequestExample>

<ResponseExample>
```json 200 OK
{
  "message": "Connection request accepted successfully.",
  "data": {
    "_id": "60c72b2f9b1e8a001f8e4c9e",
    "fromUserId": "60c72b2f9b1e8a001f8e4c9c",
    "toUserId": "60c72b2f9b1e8a001f8e4c9d",
    "status": "accepted",
    "createdAt": "2023-10-27T10:00:00.000Z",
    "updatedAt": "2023-10-27T10:05:00.000Z"
  }
}
```
```json 400 Bad Request
{
  "message": "Status not allowed!"
}
```
```json 404 Not Found
{
  "message": "Connection request not found"
}
```
</ResponseExample>

<Warning>
  This endpoint only allows reviewing requests that are currently in the "interested" state and are directed to the authenticated user.
</Warning>

## Usage Example

This section demonstrates how to use the connection request routes from a client application.

```javascript
// Example using fetch API in a JavaScript client

async function sendConnectionRequest(toUserId, status = "interested") {
  try {
    const token = localStorage.getItem("authToken"); // Assuming token is stored locally
    const response = await fetch(`/request/send/${status}/${toUserId}`, {
      method: "POST",
      headers: {
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
        "Authorization": `Bearer ${token}`,
      },
    });

    if (!response.ok) {
      const errorData = await response.json();
      throw new Error(errorData.message || `HTTP error! status: ${response.status}`);
    }

    const data = await response.json();
    console.log("Request sent successfully:", data);
    return data;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("Error sending request:", error);
  }
}

async function reviewConnectionRequest(requestId, status = "accepted") {
  try {
    const token = localStorage.getItem("authToken"); // Assuming token is stored locally
    const response = await fetch(`/request/review/${status}/${requestId}`, {
      method: "POST",
      headers: {
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
        "Authorization": `Bearer ${token}`,
      },
    });

    if (!response.ok) {
      const errorData = await response.json();
      throw new Error(errorData.message || `HTTP error! status: ${response.status}`);
    }

    const data = await response.json();
    console.log("Request reviewed successfully:", data);
    return data;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("Error reviewing request:", error);
  }
}

// Example usage:
// sendConnectionRequest("USER_ID_TO_SEND_TO");
// reviewConnectionRequest("REQUEST_ID_TO_REVIEW", "accepted");

```

## Common Errors

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="400 Bad Request - Invalid Status Type">
    This error occurs when the `status` parameter in the `/request/send` endpoint is not one of the allowed values (`ignored`, `interested`). Ensure you are passing a valid status.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="400 Bad Request - Connection Request Already Exists">
    This error is returned when a connection request between the `fromUserId` and `toUserId` already exists. You cannot send duplicate requests.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="404 Not Found - User Not Found">
    This error indicates that the `toUserId` provided in the `/request/send` endpoint does not correspond to an existing user in the database.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="404 Not Found - Connection Request Not Found">
    This error occurs in the `/request/review` endpoint if the `requestId` does not match any existing connection request, or if the request is not directed to the authenticated user, or if the request is not in the "interested" state.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>
